lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.welcome.title: Welcome aboard
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.welcome.p1.text1: So you mean to go to sea. Good. This book holds what every captain before you learned the hard way.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.welcome.p2.text1: Lost yours? Bind a new {item:pirates_n_ships:captains_almanac}**Captain's Almanac**:
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.welcome.p2.list1: Use it to read; sneak and use it on any surface to lay it down.
Turn pages with the corner arrows, the arrow keys or the mouse wheel. Escape closes it.
{#2e6a24}Green ink{/} is a tip, {#9a1c14}red ink{/} a warning, {#2a4580}blue ink{/} a link to another chapter.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.welcome.p3.text1: Some pages carry a **Show me** button: the Almanac acts the thing out on a little model ship.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.welcome.p3.text2: Or hover an item, such as the cannon, and hold the Ponder key.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.welcome.p4.text1: Start with [[pirates_n_ships:first_ship|Your first ship]]: from planks to sail in a few pages.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.welcome.p4.text2: At the back, [[pirates_n_ships:inventory|The ship's inventory]] lists every block and item, [[pirates_n_ships:ledger|The Quartermaster's ledger]] serves a server's keeper, and [[pirates_n_ships:not_yet|Not yet charted]] owns up to what is still missing.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.title: Your first ship
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p1.te: Every captain starts with planks, a helm and more courage than sense. Follow these steps.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p2.te: Build a wooden hull floating in the water.
Leave a one-block gap to the shore and every other build. Whatever touches the hull becomes part of the ship.
Natural ground (dirt, sand, raw stone, leaves) stays behind; cut and crafted blocks sail with her.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p3.te: Place a {item:pirates_n_ships:helm}**helm** on deck. The bow is where the helmsman looks.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p4.te: Raise a mast of logs or fences with two rows of {item:pirates_n_ships:yard}**yards** across it, 2 to 8 blocks apart.
Add a {item:pirates_n_ships:sail_winch}**sail winch** on deck, and a {item:pirates_n_ships:capstan}**capstan** for an anchor.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p5.te: Use the helm: everything joined to it becomes one ship. Use the winch to set sail: furled, half, full.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p6.te: Hold right-click on the helm and turn with the mouse or A and D.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p7.te: Use the capstan to drop or weigh anchor.
To unmake her, sneak and use the helm with an empty hand and press **Disassemble** twice.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.first_ship.p8.te: A seafarer village's shipwright builds sloops to order: see the **Orders** tab of the harbour master's desk, and [[pirates_n_ships:ships|Ships]].
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.title: Ships
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p1.heading: Ships
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p1.text1: Timber that agreed to float. Mend her quickly when she is hurt.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p2.heading: Launching at the helm
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p2.text1: Use a {item:pirates_n_ships:helm}**helm** to launch her: every block joined to it becomes part of her.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p2.list1_1: Air, water and natural ground never join; logs and planks do.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p2.list1_2: Up to 2048 blocks. A dock touching the hull counts, so keep a gap.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p2.text2: A **name tag** on her helm renames her.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p3.heading: The ship screen
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p3.text1: Sneak and use your helm with an empty hand. Only the owner may open it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p3.list1_1: **Ship:** her name, hull, load, sails, crew, supplies and **Disassemble**.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p3.list1_2: **Crew:** orders, and every hand's morale, station and pay.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p3.list1_3: **Stations:** who works where; **Man** sends a free hand to one.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p4.heading: Taking her apart
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p4.text1: Press **Disassemble** twice and she becomes blocks. Not while she moves, heels over 6°, or something solid is in the way.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p4.text2: A ship whose helm is broken cannot be steered or taken apart until you place a new helm on her deck.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p5.heading: The dry hold
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p5.text1: Rooms below the lowest place water could pour in stay dry.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p5.list1_2: **Leaky:** fences, walls, bars, panes, ladders, chains.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p5.list1_3: **Doors, trapdoors, fence gates:** watertight only when shut.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p5.text2: Dry volume keeps her up; flood water drags her down.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p6.heading: Flooding
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p6.text1: A hull block destroyed below the waterline is a breach, and an open door or hatch there lets the sea in too.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p6.text2: Rooms joined by an open door fill together. Any block placed in the breach stops the flow.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p6.text3: Under the flood water you hold your breath, as in the sea.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p7.heading: Pumps
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p7.text1: Place a {item:pirates_n_ships:bilge_pump}**bilge pump** on the hold floor or the deck above it, and hold right-click to drain the highest flooded room below.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p7.text2: Pumping is hungry work: order a hand to **Man the pumps**.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p8.heading: Patching a breach
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p8.text1: Stand inside, look at the edge of the hole and use a {item:pirates_n_ships:hull_patch}**hull patch**. The water stops at once.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p9.heading: When she breaks in two
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p9.text1: Shoot through the only block joining two parts and she splits. The part with the helm stays your ship; the other drifts as a wreck.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p9.text2: A {item:pirates_n_ships:shipwright_toolkit}**shipwright's toolkit** nails her together again.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p10.text1: The toolkit needs a {item:pirates_n_ships:carpenters_hammer}**carpenter's hammer** and a {item:pirates_n_ships:saw}**saw**.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p11.text1: Add leather, and {item:pirates_n_ships:nails}**nails**: each repair takes 4.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p12.text1: **1.** Sneak and use the toolkit on the part you keep. Green sparkles show where pieces meet.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p12.text2: **2.** Bring the broken piece against her, straight and face to face. Bridge a one-block gap with planks.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p12.text3: **3.** Use the toolkit on the broken piece, and she is whole.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p12.text4: Only pieces of the same ship join, of up to 200 blocks each.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p13.text1: A {item:pirates_n_ships:nameplate}**name board** (any sign and a gold nugget make three) fixed on her side shows her name once she is launched and named; boards side by side join, and the name grows across the row.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p14.text1: A figurehead hangs on the bow block you click and looks toward you. The {item:pirates_n_ships:figurehead_mermaid}**mermaid** and the {item:pirates_n_ships:figurehead_lion}**lion**:
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p16.text1: An {item:pirates_n_ships:oak_railing}**oak railing** runs along a block's edge; click again to rail another edge.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p16.text2: A {item:pirates_n_ships:oak_railing_port}**railing port** is the gap in it: cannons fire through it, boarders cross there.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p17.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:ship_lantern}**ship's lantern** hangs or stands, and burns even under water.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p17.text2: {item:pirates_n_ships:rope_coil}**Rope coils** stack four to a spot.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p18.text1: {item:pirates_n_ships:stern_window}**Stern windows** go into a wall from outside; right-click to work the shutters.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p18.text2: The {item:pirates_n_ships:chart_table}**chart table** is a captain's table with a chart spread on it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p19.text1: Sleep in a {item:pirates_n_ships:sea_cot}**sea cot** aboard and you respawn at it wherever she has gone.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p20.text1: Seafarer villages build ships to order. The **Orders** tab of the harbour master's desk shows each ship's price, days and materials.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p20.text2: **1.** Bring the doubloons and materials and press **Order** for a {item:pirates_n_ships:ship_receipt}**ship receipt** that counts the days.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p20.text3: **2.** When it reads "Ready for pickup", use the desk with the receipt in hand.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p20.text4: **3.** She waits at a berth by the pier.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p20.text5: Armed sloops are never for sale: earn one by rank or take one at sea ([[pirates_n_ships:law|Law]], [[pirates_n_ships:combat|Weapons and combat]]).
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ships.p21.list1_: Keep near the middle of the world: very far out, ships stop moving true.
A ship floats only on water beneath her own hull.
Cargo and flood water make her list and sit lower.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.title: Sailing
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p1.text1: Learn the wind, learn your canvas, and keep the bow where you want it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p2.text1: One wind blows for every soul at sea. It veers and freshens slowly through the day; rain and thunder stiffen it. Read it from the white streaks on the water, from flags and from bellying sails.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p2.text2: Aboard, a pale arrow on your compass rose shows where the wind comes from. The longer the arrow, the stronger the wind; it glows amber in a gust.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p3.text1: A square sail hangs between two {item:pirates_n_ships:yard}**yards**, rows of yard blocks laid across the ship. The middle block marks the mast.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p3.text2: Both yards stand one block forward of the mast, in the column in front of it, never in the mast's own column. So the cloth hangs before the mast, as on any ship at sea.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p3.text3: **1.** Set the upper yard across the ship, its middle block just forward of the mast.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p3.text4: **2.** Set a second yard the same way, 2 to 8 blocks straight below it, with only air or mast between their middles.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p3.text5: **3.** The pair is now one sail. You place no canvas: the cloth is drawn between them.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p4.text1: A square sail loves a wind from astern and is useless close to the wind. Longer yards set further apart make a bigger sail, and three yards on one mast make two sails.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p4.text2: Click a yard that heads no sail and it tells you what is wrong with the rig.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p5.text1: A triangular sail is rigged with {item:pirates_n_ships:rope}**rope** and three {item:pirates_n_ships:cleat}**cleats**. It is the sail for a wind on the beam.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p5.text2: **1.** Put one cleat high on the side of the mast: the head.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p5.text3: **2.** Put one further forward and lower, on the deck or a bowsprit: the tack.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p5.text4: **3.** Put one straight below the head: the clew.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p5.text5: **4.** Use a rope on the head cleat, then on the tack cleat. A stay runs between them and the cloth fills the triangle.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p5.text6: A rope between two cleats or mooring rings that is no stay becomes a sagging rope line, for a rail or rigging.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p6.text1: Every sail has three trims: furled, half and full. Use the {item:pirates_n_ships:sail_winch}**sail winch** on deck to work every sail at once, or click an upper yard or a head cleat with an empty hand to work that sail alone.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p6.text2: No sail drives straight into the wind. A sail that shakes and hangs slack is in the no-go zone: bear away. Your crew braces the yards for you.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p7.show_: Show me: steering at the helm
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p7.text1: Hold right-click on the {item:pirates_n_ships:helm}**helm** to take the wheel, then move the mouse or hold A and D to turn: right or D to starboard, left or A to port. Let go and the wheel stays put.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p7.text2: The line above your hotbar shows the rudder angle. The rudder bites only while she moves through the water, and works the other way round when she goes astern.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p8.text1: Wind on the sails heels her over and the hull rights itself; near her limit the sails spill their wind. A wide, shallow hull stands stiffest.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p8.text2: She is ballasted as you built her. What you load later can make her list: trim the cargo and pump her dry, as [[pirates_n_ships:trade|Cargo and trade]] explains.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p9.show_: Show me: dropping and weighing anchor
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p9.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:capstan}**capstan** works the anchor, which hangs outside the hull on its side. Use it to let go, and again to weigh.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p9.text2: Once the anchor bites, she swings to lie head to her chain. Over water too deep for the chain, the capstan refuses to let go.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p9.text3: A ship pulling harder than her anchor holds drags it. Furl before you anchor.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p10.head: Mooring
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p10.text: A moored ship is simply a ship lying still at her berth: bring her in slowly and drop the anchor.

{item:pirates_n_ships:mooring_ring}**Mooring rings** and cleats serve the grappling hook. A hook catches on a ring and holds longer there; use a ring or cleat on your own ship to make a hooked ship fast. See [[pirates_n_ships:combat|Weapons and combat]].
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p11.head: The gangway
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p11.text: The {item:pirates_n_ships:boarding_plank}**boarding plank** bridges your deck and the quay. Use it on the edge of either, toward the other: it lies as one straight board, up or down to a high pier, up to six blocks.
It goes where the ship goes, but let her drift along the quay and it breaks. Sneak and use it with an empty hand to stow it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p12.head: Waves and weather
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p12.text: Fair weather brings a low swell, rain rough seas, a thunderstorm high crests. A small boat rides them far more than a big one.
In rough seas every open hatch or low rim near the waterline takes water. Close your hatches and man a pump before a storm.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p13.head: Ratlines
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p13.text: {item:pirates_n_ships:ratlines}**Ratlines** are rope nets for climbing aloft.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p13.list: Click the side of a mast to hang a net like a ladder.
Click the deck or the gunwale to lay a sloped net, rising the way you face.
Click a ratline to add the next one to its run. Sneak to place against the clicked side.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p13.text: A net needs something to rest on: break one and those hanging from it fall too.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p14.head: Ratline nets
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p14.text: A {item:pirates_n_ships:ratline_net}**ratline net** runs from a {item:pirates_n_ships:chainplate}**chainplate** on the rail to a {item:pirates_n_ships:mast_hoop}**mast hoop** up the mast. Use the net on one, then on the other; the line between them must be clear.
Walk into the net and hold forward or jump to climb; sneak to hold on. String several chainplates to one hoop and the space between them is netted too.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p15.head: Chainplate and hoop
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p15.text: Break a net, its chainplate or put a block into it and that net comes down. Break the hoop and they all do.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p16.head: The ship's bell
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p16.text: The {item:pirates_n_ships:ships_bell}**ship's bell** sits on a post or a wall. Right-click it and it rings. It does not call your crew, but in a harbour every bell rings the alarm when raiders come.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p17.head: The crow's nest
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p17.text: The {item:pirates_n_ships:crows_nest}**crow's nest** is a barrel for the masthead, set on a log, fence, wall or any solid top. Climb in over the rim; sneak to stay put.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p18.head: The lookout
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p18.text: Whoever stands in the nest keeps the lookout, you or a hand you post with the whistle. The lookout calls what is new to everyone aboard:
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p18.list: **Ships,** by their flag: merchant, navy, pirate, wreck or just a sail.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p18.text: Each call rings a small bell and lights a diamond on your compass: white for land, red for a pirate, blue for the navy.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p19.head: The ship's panels
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p19.text: While you are aboard, two panels watch over her:
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p19.list: **The compass,** bottom left: heading, wind, speed in knots and rudder angle.
**The hull strip,** bottom right: one cell per compartment, filling blue as water comes in, with a red mark at a breach.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.sailing.p19.text: Her name, load and crew are on the ship screen at the helm; see [[pirates_n_ships:ships|Ships]].
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.title: Crew
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p1.heading: Crew
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p1.text1: One captain cannot work the winch, the helm, the pumps and the guns at once. A crew can.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p1.text2: Hire hands, feed, pay and bunk them, and they sail her for you. The {item:pirates_n_ships:captains_whistle}**captain's whistle** gives the orders.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.heading: Hiring hands
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.text1: The **Crew** tab of a harbour master's desk lists who seeks a berth. Each asks a fee, then a daily wage.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.list1_1: **Sailors**, at seafarer villages: 10 doubloons. Not for a captain the villagers refuse to trade with.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.list1_2: **Navy ratings**, at navy outposts: 15. Enlisted officers only.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.list1_3: **Pirates**, at pirate islands: 20. Only for a friend of the pirates, or a Buccaneer or worse.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.text2: Bring your ship within about 32 blocks of the port first: the new hand walks straight aboard.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p2.text3: Every hand needs a free {item:pirates_n_ships:hammock}**hammock**. The desk refuses a hand you cannot bunk.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p3.heading: Stations
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p3.text1: A station is a block a hand can work: the {item:pirates_n_ships:sail_winch}**sail winch**, the **helm**, the {item:pirates_n_ships:capstan}**capstan**, the {item:pirates_n_ships:bilge_pump}**bilge pump**, the {item:pirates_n_ships:cannon}**cannon**, the {item:pirates_n_ships:swivel_gun}**swivel gun** and the {item:pirates_n_ships:crows_nest}**crow's nest**.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p3.text2: A posted hand walks to his station, even under way, and stays there while she sails.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.heading: The captain's whistle
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.list1_1: Use it on a hand, then on a station: he takes that station.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.list1_2: Use it on a hand at a station: he is released.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.list1_3: Sneak and use it on a hand: he is dismissed. Only you, or whoever hired him, may do so.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.list1_4: Use it in the air: the order wheel opens. Click an order, or hold the use key, aim and let go.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.text1: The wheel: **Hoist**, **Reef** and **Furl sails**, **Man the pumps**, **Fire!**, **Load!**, **Fire at will**, **Drop** and **Weigh anchor**, **Release crew**.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p4.text2: The ship screen at the helm gives the same orders. See [[pirates_n_ships:ships|Ships]].
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p5.heading: Orders, not assignments
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p5.text1: Blow an order and free hands on deck man the nearest unmanned stations that can carry it out. A hand you posted yourself is never moved.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p5.text2: If nobody can, you are told why.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p5.text3: **Release crew** sends everyone off and ends **Fire at will**.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p6.heading: A helmsman
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p6.text1: A hand at the helm steers the course he is given, but leaves the sails alone: order **Hoist sails** as well. Take the wheel and he lets go.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p7.heading: Hammocks
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p7.text1: Hang a hammock between two supports at the same height, such as posts, walls or the hull side: click the block next to one while looking toward the other.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p7.text2: At nightfall every hand off station turns in to the nearest free hammock. A night in one cheers him; a night aboard without one does not.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p8.heading: Your own bunk
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p8.text1: Right-click a free hammock at night to sleep in it as in a bed, even under way. Your respawn point sails with the ship.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p8.text2: A {item:pirates_n_ships:sea_cot}**sea cot** is the captain's bed for the great cabin, and works the same way.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.heading: Morale and wages
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.text1: Every hand has a morale from 0 to 100; use the whistle on him to read it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.list1_1: A night in a hammock: up. Without one: down.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.list1_3: Hungry or thirsty: down every day, and slower at work.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.list1_4: Rum: up. Scurvy: down every day.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p9.text2: Every dawn each hand eats from the [[pirates_n_ships:provisions|Provisions]] and wants 2 doubloons, paid from the chests and crates aboard, then from your purse.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p10.heading: Desertion
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p10.text1: A hand below 20 morale for two dawns means to desert: he tells you, then walks off at the next port. Lift his spirits above 20 and he stays.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p10.text2: On some seas a miserable crew rises in mutiny and takes the ship. Your server tells you whether yours is one.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.heading: Fire at will
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.text1: On **Fire at will** your gun crews fire at the nearest hostile ship within 64 blocks. Your flag decides who is hostile:
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.list1_1: Navy flag: the Jolly Roger, and ships found out under false colours.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.list1_2: Jolly Roger: navy ships, merchants and unflagged ships.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.list1_3: Merchant flag or none: only the Jolly Roger.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.crew.p11.text2: Turn her to bring the guns to bear; see [[pirates_n_ships:combat|Weapons and combat]].
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.title: Flags
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p1.heading: Flags
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p1.text1: A flag tells every ship on the horizon who you are, and the sea holds you to it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p2.heading: The colours
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p2.list1_1: {item:pirates_n_ships:merchant_flag}**Merchant flag**, or none: neutral to all.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p2.list1_2: {item:pirates_n_ships:navy_flag}**Navy flag**: navy and merchants are friends, pirates foes.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p2.list1_3: **Any banner:** your own flag, neutral to all.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p3.heading: The Jolly Roger
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p3.text1: Under the {item:pirates_n_ships:jolly_roger_flag}**Jolly Roger** the pirates let you be and merchants may strike to you. The navy fires on everyone aboard on sight, and being seen under it is a crime.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p4.heading: The flagpole
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p4.text1: A {item:pirates_n_ships:flagpole}**flagpole** flies the flag downwind from its top, a block high and a block and a half long, so leave it room.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p4.list1_1: **Use it with a flag:** the flag flies after three seconds; you get the old one back.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p4.list1_2: **Empty hand:** strike the colours, or raise them again.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p4.list1_3: **Sneak, empty hand:** take the flag down.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p5.heading: Tall poles
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p5.text1: Stack flagpoles into one pole up to 6 blocks tall. The top flies the flag, and you may work it from any block.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p5.text2: A {item:pirates_n_ships:flag_pedestal}**flag pedestal** is a sturdy foot: set it on solid ground and stand a pole in it. Breaking it brings the whole pole down.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p6.heading: False colours
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p6.text1: A ship flies the highest flag on her poles. Under the navy flag you pass the navy while your record is clean, but a suspect may be found out by any navy soldier in sight. Then you are charged heavily and hunted for five minutes.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p6.text2: Firing on struck colours, a merchant flag or a banner is a crime, and your crew's shots are charged to you.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p7.heading: Striking your colours
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p7.text1: Strike your flag to surrender: navy and pirates stop attacking. Raise the Jolly Roger again and the chase is back on. See [[pirates_n_ships:law|Law]].
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p8.heading: Dyed sails
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.flags.p8.text1: Use a dye on the upper yard of a square sail, or the head cleat of a triangular one, to colour the cloth; white dye brings back plain canvas. A large square sail takes a banner the same way. Colours are only for show.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.title: Provisions
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p1.te: An empty pantry sinks more ships than cannon ever did. Every dawn your crew takes a day's food and water from the stores aboard.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p2.te: The {item:pirates_n_ships:pantry}**pantry** is the ship's food store, opening like a chest. Anything edible counts; a hand eats about a loaf of bread a day.
Sneak and use it empty-handed to read what it holds. A hopper below takes out only the waste.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p3.te: Fresh food spoils after five days in the pantry.
Preserved food never spoils: bread, dried kelp, honey and the sailor's own {item:pirates_n_ships:hardtack}**hardtack**.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p4.te: {item:pirates_n_ships:salted_fish}**Salted fish** and {item:pirates_n_ships:salt_pork}**salt pork** keep as long as you sail.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p5.te: A {item:pirates_n_ships:water_barrel}**water barrel** holds 16 rations, and each hand drinks one a day. It comes off the bench full.
Buckets and bottles fill or empty it, and rain tops it up.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p6.te: Hungry hands work at three quarters pace, thirsty ones at half. Three days without food, or one without water, and the whole crew deserts.
After eight days without fresh food comes scurvy. Fresh food cures it, fruit best.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p7.te: While there is {item:pirates_n_ships:rum}**rum** aboard, each hand gets a daily ration and cheers up. Stow ten days' worth or more and they drink double and work slowly.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p8.te: Swimming in cold or frozen seas soon freezes you. A boat, a deck, leather armour or a swig of rum keeps you warm.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.provisions.p9.te: Prisoners in your brig eat and drink half a hand's share, and get no rum. See [[pirates_n_ships:law|Law]].
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.title: Cargo and trade
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p1.heading: Cargo and trade
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p1.text1: Buy cheap, carry it where it is wanted, and sell it dear. That is the whole of honest trade.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p2.heading: Crates and barrels
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p2.text1: Bulk cargo goes in containers that hold great amounts of **one kind of item**.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p2.list1_2: {item:pirates_n_ships:cargo_barrel}**Cargo barrel:** 1536 items, whatever their stack size; best for rum.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p3.heading: Stowing
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p3.list1_1: Use with a stack to put it in, with an empty hand to take a stack out.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p3.list1_2: Sneak-use with an empty hand to put in everything of that kind you carry.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p3.list1_3: A broken container keeps its cargo, and hoppers work on it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p3.text1: Items that do not stack are refused, and stolen and clean goods never share a container.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p4.heading: Weight and trim
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p4.text1: Cargo weighs: containers grow heavier as they fill, and a chest presses down where it stands.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p4.text2: Keep heavy cargo low, spread and amidships. A laden ship sits deeper, floods sooner and is slower to turn.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p4.text3: The ship screen at the helm reads her load, from Light to Overloaded.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p5.heading: The sea chest
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p5.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:sea_chest}**sea chest** holds 54 stacks and keeps them when broken, carried or floated.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p5.list1_1: Use it in the air to carry it on your back: slow, no jumping or swimming.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p5.list1_2: Place it on water and it floats with wind and current.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p5.list1_3: Sneak-use to pick it up; strike it to knock it loose.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p6.heading: The paddle
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p6.text1: Use a {item:pirates_n_ships:paddle}**paddle** on a floating sea chest to sit on the lid and paddle it like a little boat. Sneak to get off.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p7.heading: Doubloons
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p7.text1: The gold {item:pirates_n_ships:doubloon}**doubloon** is the coin of the sea. You earn it by trading, from pirates' purses, wrecks and buried treasure, and from bounties, contracts and quests.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p7.text2: Keep them in your inventory; markets take them from there.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p8.heading: Harbours
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p8.text1: Every port has a harbour master's desk.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p8.list1_1: **Seafarer villages:** quay, pier, cottages and a tavern on a beach.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p8.list1_2: **Navy outposts:** rarer stone forts with cannon and a garrison.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p8.list1_3: **Pirate islands:** rarer still, camps under the Jolly Roger. Strangers are not welcome.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p9.heading: The harbour master
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p9.text1: Right-click the harbour master or his {item:pirates_n_ships:harbor_desk}**harbour master's desk** to open the market. A desk you place inside a port joins that port.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p10.list1_: **Goods:** buy and sell. Green goods are cheap here, orange goods wanted here.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p10.text1: Stay near the desk, or the market closes.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p11.text1: Buying raises a price and selling lowers it; prices drift back day by day. Carry a good from a port that makes it to one that wants it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p11.text2: Spices fetch the most. Tropical ports grow sugar, cocoa, {item:pirates_n_ships:tobacco}**tobacco** and {item:pirates_n_ships:spices}**spices**; colder ports deal in fish, timber and iron. {item:pirates_n_ships:cloth}**Cloth** you can weave yourself.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p12.text1: Goods from a captured or sunk ship carry a plunder mark. Only a pirate fence buys them, cheaply and with no questions.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p12.text2: Honest harbour masters report plunder to the navy, and a navy ship or fort that sees much of it in your hold suspects you of piracy.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p13.text1: A navy outpost charges a small fee when your ship berths or anchors there, once a day. Leave it unpaid and its desk will not trade with you. Trusted captains and officers dock free.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p14.text1: A **contract** asks you to carry goods to another port by a deadline. You pay a deposit and get it back with the reward.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.trade.p14.text2: **Quests** pay doubloons and standing: hunts, prisoners, cargo runs, treasure hunts, escorts, raids and patrols. Each desk offers a few at a time, each with a deadline.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.title: Law
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p1.heading: Law
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p1.text1: The Crown keeps a ledger on every soul at sea. Stay honest and the navy is your friend; turn pirate and you had better be fast.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.heading: Your record
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.text1: Every crime adds to your record: theft, violence, plunder aboard, false colours and, worst of all, piracy and desertion.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.text2: From 10 you are a **suspect**, from 50 **wanted**, from 200 **notorious**. Keep clean and it fades day by day.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p2.text3: Theft counts only when someone sees it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p3.heading: Fines and bounties
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p3.text1: Right-click a navy officer with doubloons to pay off your record. He will not deal with a wanted man, and no coin buys a pardon for the notorious.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p3.text2: A wanted man carries a bounty. Kill him and bring the {item:pirates_n_ships:bounty_proof}**bounty proof** to a navy officer; alive pays more.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p4.heading: The notice board
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p4.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:notice_board}**notice board** lists every bounty, and places your own.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p5.heading: Shackles
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p5.text1: {item:pirates_n_ships:shackles}**Shackles** take a beaten foe alive: use them on a creature at a quarter of its health or less. Bosses cannot be taken.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p6.heading: Prisoners
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p6.list1_1: A prisoner stops fighting and never wanders off.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p6.list1_2: Use the shackles on it again to lead it, or to let go.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p6.list1_3: Left alone outside a cell, it tries to slip away.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p6.text1: Right-click a navy officer with an empty hand, prisoners close by, to turn them in or ransom them. Your shackles come back.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p7.heading: Press-ganging
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p7.text1: Right-click a shackled sailor on your own ship with the {item:pirates_n_ships:captains_whistle}**captain's whistle** to press-gang him into your crew. He comes aboard sullen, and it is a crime.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p7.text2: Sneak-use your own prisoner with an empty hand to set him free.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p8.heading: The brig
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p8.text1: A {item:pirates_n_ships:brig_door}**brig door** locks and unlocks with a {item:pirates_n_ships:brig_key}**brig key**. Locked, it opens only for whoever placed it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p9.heading: Bars and keys
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p9.text1: {item:pirates_n_ships:brig_bars}**Brig bars** connect like iron bars. A prisoner shut in a small space by blocks, bars and a locked brig door is **in a cell** and stays put.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p9.text2: Any brig key opens any brig door. Keep keys away from your prisoners.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p10.heading: The three powers
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p10.text1: The navy, the pirates and the villagers each remember you, from −100 to 100.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p10.list1_1: Killing pirates pleases the navy; plunder pleases the pirates; trade pleases the villagers.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p10.list1_2: Good standing means better prices. Villagers stop trading at −60.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p10.list1_3: Liked pirates leave you be until you strike first. At −60 the navy fires on sight.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p11.heading: Navy patrols
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p11.text1: Navy patrols chase the Jolly Roger, false colours they see through, and wanted men.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p11.text2: Strike your colours and their guns fall silent. Outrun them and they give up.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p12.heading: Careers
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p12.text1: You may climb only one ladder.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p12.list1_1: **The navy:** enlist with an officer once the navy trusts you, and rise from Midshipman to Admiral.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p12.list1_2: **Infamy:** plunder and taken ships make you a Buccaneer, a Dread Captain and a Pirate Lord.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p12.list1_3: **Letter of marque:** bought from a navy officer; pirates you kill earn prize money.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p13.heading: Rewards of rank
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p13.list1_1: **Lieutenant:** the navy flag, free docking at navy outposts, and an officer's uniform and saber.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p13.list1_2: **Navy Captain:** a {item:pirates_n_ships:ship_commission}**ship commission** for an armed sloop, and cheaper ships at navy desks.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p13.list1_3: **Dread Captain:** a pirate sloop from a pirate island's fence.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.law.p13.text1: Your title rides before your name in chat and over your head.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.title: Weapons and combat
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p1.text1: Sooner or later someone will want your ship, your cargo or your head. Learn the blade, the pistol and the great guns before you need them.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p2.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:cutlass}**cutlass** is heavy and wide, made for the slash.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p3.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:rapier}**rapier** is light and long, made for the thrust.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p3.text2: The {item:pirates_n_ships:saber}**saber** is the officer's blade, good at both.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p4.list1_: **Slash:** a quick left click. A wide, short arc.
**Thrust:** hold left click a moment, then release. Narrow, longer and harder, but slow to recover if it misses.
**Guard:** hold right click. It stops every blow from the front, at a cost in stamina. Blows from behind or the side get through.
**Parry:** tap right click just before a blow lands. The attacker staggers and you may **riposte** for extra harm.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p4.text1: While you hold a sword, right click belongs to the blade. Put it away to open a door or take the helm.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p5.text1: A brass-framed bar shows your stamina. Attacks, guarding and missed parries drain it; rest refills it. Empty, you can neither guard nor parry.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p5.text2: Pirates fight as you do. Parry when the arm goes up or back, but beware the feint that baits an early parry.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p6.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:pistol}**pistol** is a single-shot flintlock. Its ball scatters.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p7.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:musket}**musket** hits harder and flies flatter and truer. Both fire {item:pirates_n_ships:lead_shot}**lead shot** with gunpowder.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p8.text1: **1.** **Load:** with shot and powder in your pack, hold right click: three seconds for the pistol, five for the musket.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p8.text2: **2.** **Aim:** hold right click. After a second of steady aim the shot tightens.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p8.text3: **3.** **Fire:** left click. From the hip the ball scatters wide.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p8.text4: Letting go of right click never fires. Sneak to lower an aimed gun.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p8.text5: In the rain a quarter of your shots misfire; the charge stays in.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p9.text1: Click the deck where the **front** of the carriage should stand, by the rail: the barrel overhangs one block ahead. Both halves need a block beneath them.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p9.text2: A cannon cannot turn sideways. Lay your ship so her broadside bears.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p10.text2: **2.** **Aim:** sneak and use it with an empty hand. The upper half raises the barrel, the lower half lowers it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p10.text3: **3.** **Fire:** use it with an empty hand.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p11.text1: The barrel needs five seconds to cool. A ball smashes the wood it strikes, and a hole below the waterline lets the sea in. Hit square; a grazing ball glances off.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p12.text1: Both load like a ball, after the powder. {item:pirates_n_ships:chain_shot}**Chain shot** breaks no hull but tears sails, cuts ropes and breaks ratlines. Torn cloth mends slowly by itself.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p12.text2: {item:pirates_n_ships:grapeshot}**Grapeshot** bursts into a cone of pellets that hurt men and break nothing. Sweep a crowded deck before you board.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p13.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:swivel_gun}**swivel gun** mounts on a fence, a wall, bars or any full block. Load it like a cannon, then hold right click with an empty hand: it follows your eye and fires when you let go.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p14.text1: Post a hand at a gun with the whistle and stock powder and shot in a chest, barrel or crate within 4 blocks on the same ship. Blow **Load!**, then **Fire!**: every manned, loaded gun fires, and the crew reloads it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p14.text2: **Fire at will** lets the crews pick targets; see [[pirates_n_ships:crew|Crew]].
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p15.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:grappling_hook}**grappling hook** bites into ships and land. Right click to throw it, with 32 blocks of rope. Or hold it in your off hand, load it into a musket and fire it, with 64 blocks.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p16.list1: **Two ships:** hooked from your own ship, the rope hauls them side by side.
**Haul:** hold sneak with the rope in hand and walk back.
**Climb:** right-click your own rope when the hook is two blocks or more above you.
**Make fast:** use a cleat or mooring ring of yours while the hook is out.
**Let go:** sneak and use with an empty hand.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p16.text1: It slips off water, leaves, glass panes and creatures.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p17.text1: Use a rope made fast to a cleat or ring to slide down it, from your masthead onto her deck.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p17.text2: With the ships alongside, use a {item:pirates_n_ships:boarding_plank}**boarding plank** on top of your gunwale. Keep the ships together or it breaks. Hold the plank and look at your rail: the board it would lay shows in green, and a red cell marks what stands in the way.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p18.text1: Merchantmen, navy patrols and pirates sail the sea lanes.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p18.list1: Take goods from her hold while aboard: plundered.
Sink her with the last shot: the deed is yours.
Kill every fighter and hold her deck: she is yours, crew and all.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p18.text2: Taking a merchant is piracy. See [[pirates_n_ships:law|Law]].
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p19.list1: **Pirates** attack you and the navy on sight.
**Navy soldiers** shoot at you only when you are wanted.
**Navy officers** are deadly with the saber.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p19.text1: Striking navy men is a crime; killing pirates is not.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p20.text1: Every pirate island has a captain with a bounty of 300 doubloons. Sneak and use him with a sword in hand to call a duel; his crew keeps out of it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p20.text2: Slain, he drops his hat, a treasure map and your bounty proof.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p21.text1: Linger at a navy outpost or seafarer village and pirates may raid it. Kill every raider to beat them off.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p22.text1: Hats and coats are armour too; a hat gives one point. The {item:pirates_n_ships:captains_hat}**captain's hat** you only win from a pirate captain. The {item:pirates_n_ships:pirate_hat}**pirate hat**:
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p24.text1: In navy blue and white: the {item:pirates_n_ships:officer_hat}**officer's bicorne** and the {item:pirates_n_ships:officers_coat}**officer's coat**, three points.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p25.text1: The {item:pirates_n_ships:officers_breeches}**officer's breeches**, two points, and {item:pirates_n_ships:officers_boots}**boots**, one.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p26.text1: In charcoal and gold: the {item:pirates_n_ships:captains_coat}**captain's coat** and {item:pirates_n_ships:captains_breeches}**breeches**.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p28.text1: The **kraken** rises beside ships in the deep ocean, most often at night and in storms. It drags hulls down and smashes masts. Strike its eyes.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p28.text2: It leaves a {item:pirates_n_ships:kraken_beak}**kraken beak** and {item:pirates_n_ships:kraken_ink}**kraken ink**.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p29.text1: Sharks hunt swimmers, and blood drives them into a frenzy. Stay on deck or in a boat and they leave you alone.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p30.text1: In a storm at sea a **waterspout** pulls in and lifts what comes near, and tears set sails. Steer clear, or furl first.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.combat.p30.text2: In the deep ocean a **whirlpool** drags boats and swimmers under and turns ships about.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.title: Charts and navigation
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p1.text1: A captain who does not know where he is soon knows where the rocks are. Keep your chart and mark it well.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p2.text1: Your {item:pirates_n_ships:chart}**chart** draws itself as you sail, inking in the coasts, shallows and open sea of the overworld around you.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p2.list1_: Use it, or press **M** with it in hand, to open the map.
Drag to pan, scroll to zoom.
Right-click to place a named marker; click one to change it.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p3.text1: Set {item:pirates_n_ships:map_tile}**map tiles** side by side on a wall or table, all facing one way, to make a board.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p4.text1: **1.** Use a tile with your chart in hand.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p4.text2: **2.** Drag the frame over the waters you want and pick a zoom.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p4.text4: Each tile costs an ink sac; one {item:pirates_n_ships:kraken_ink}**kraken ink** pays for eight. Anyone who has charted more can press **Update** to fill in the blanks.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p5.text1: The lookout calls points of the compass from the bow, 32 to the circle:
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p5.list1_: **Two points off the starboard bow:** a little right of ahead.
**On the beam:** square off the side.
**Abaft the beam:** behind it, toward the stern.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p6.text1: Pirate fences sell blank {item:pirates_n_ships:treasure_map}**treasure maps**, and wrecks hold some. Use one and it marks the nearest unfound treasure.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p6.text2: Hold it to see the red X and the way there. At the X, dig into the sand for the chest.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p6.text3: Every pirate island has a chest buried beneath two crossed logs.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.charts.p7.text1: The ocean floor is strewn with wrecks, each with a chest of ship's stores: doubloons, rum, supplies, now and then a treasure map. Tall wrecks lie in deep water. Bring something to breathe and see down there.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.title: The ship's inventory
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p1.tex: Every block and item a hand may need, a line on each, and the chapter that tells the rest.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p2.lis: {item:pirates_n_ships:helm}**Helm:** launches, steers and takes apart a ship. [[pirates_n_ships:ships|Ships]]
{item:pirates_n_ships:yard}**Yard:** a spar; two on a mast make a square sail. [[pirates_n_ships:sailing|Sailing]]
{item:pirates_n_ships:cleat}**Cleat:** holds a stay, a rope line or a grappling rope.
{item:pirates_n_ships:rope}**Rope:** rigs stays and rope lines.
{item:pirates_n_ships:sail_winch}**Sail winch:** works every sail aboard. A station.
{item:pirates_n_ships:capstan}**Capstan:** drops and weighs the anchor. A station.
{item:pirates_n_ships:mooring_ring}**Mooring ring:** catches and holds a grappling hook.
{item:pirates_n_ships:ratlines}**Ratlines:** rope nets for climbing aloft.
{item:pirates_n_ships:crows_nest}**Crow's nest:** the lookout's barrel. A station.
{item:pirates_n_ships:ships_bell}**Ship's bell:** rings when struck.
{item:pirates_n_ships:bilge_pump}**Bilge pump:** pumps a flooded hold. A station.
{item:pirates_n_ships:hull_patch}**Hull patch:** closes a breach.
{item:pirates_n_ships:flagpole}**Flagpole:** flies your colours. [[pirates_n_ships:flags|Flags]]
{item:pirates_n_ships:flag_pedestal}**Flag pedestal:** a carved plinth a flagpole stands in.
{item:pirates_n_ships:nameplate}**Name Board:** shows her name across the boards it joins.

{item:pirates_n_ships:figurehead_mermaid}{item:pirates_n_ships:figurehead_lion}{item:pirates_n_ships:figurehead_eagle}{item:pirates_n_ships:figurehead_skull}**Figureheads:** a mermaid, lion, eagle or skull for the bow.
{item:pirates_n_ships:ship_lantern}**Ship's lantern:** a lantern that burns under water.
{item:pirates_n_ships:stern_window}**Stern window:** shuttered windows for the great cabin.
{item:pirates_n_ships:rope_coil}**Rope coil:** coiled rope for the deck.
{item:pirates_n_ships:chart_table}**Chart table:** a captain's table.
{item:pirates_n_ships:sea_cot}**Sea cot:** the captain's bed at sea.
{item:pirates_n_ships:hammock}**Hammock:** a bunk for one hand. [[pirates_n_ships:crew|Crew]]
{item:pirates_n_ships:boarding_plank}**Boarding plank:** a bridge to an enemy deck.

{item:pirates_n_ships:oak_railing}{item:pirates_n_ships:oak_railing_port}**Railing, railing port:** a rail along a block's edge; click again to rail another. A cannon fires and a boarding plank goes out through the port.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p3.lis: {item:pirates_n_ships:cargo_crate}**Cargo crate:** 32 stacks of one item. [[pirates_n_ships:trade|Cargo and trade]]
{item:pirates_n_ships:hardtack}**Hardtack,** {item:pirates_n_ships:salted_fish}**salted fish,** {item:pirates_n_ships:salt_pork}**salt pork:** food that never spoils.
{item:pirates_n_ships:rum}**Rum:** cheers a crew and warms a swimmer.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p4.lis: {item:pirates_n_ships:lead_shot}**Lead shot:** a ball for pistol or musket.
{item:pirates_n_ships:swivel_gun}**Swivel gun:** a small gun on a yoke. A station.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p5.lis: {item:pirates_n_ships:bounty_proof}**Bounty proof:** proof of a kill; hand it to a navy officer.
{item:pirates_n_ships:ship_commission}**Ship commission:** an armed sloop earned by rank.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p6.lis: {item:pirates_n_ships:map_tile}**Map tile:** a board for a drawn chart.

{item:pirates_n_ships:shipwright_toolkit}**Shipwright's toolkit,** from the {item:pirates_n_ships:carpenters_hammer}**carpenter's hammer,** {item:pirates_n_ships:saw}**saw** and {item:pirates_n_ships:nails}**nails:** joins a broken ship.
{item:pirates_n_ships:kraken_beak}**Kraken beak,** {item:pirates_n_ships:kraken_ink}**kraken ink:** spoils of the deep.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.inventory.p7.tex: All of them, with spawn eggs for the folk and beasts of the sea, are in the "Pirates 'n' Ships" creative tab.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.title: The Quartermaster's ledger
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p1.text1: These pages are for the keeper of a server, not the hand at the wheel: the settings a keeper reaches for first, and the orders an operator may give.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p2.text1: Open them under Mods, then Pirates 'n' Ships, then Config (on Fabric with Mod Menu). Gameplay sits in the server config, which every client receives; looks and sounds sit in each player's client config.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p2.text2: Every feature has a switch and every strength a value. Below: section.name, default after the colon.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p3.list1_: assembly.max\_blocks: 2048. The largest ship a helm launches.
ship\_screen.enabled: true. Off, sneak-using the helm takes the ship apart at once.
helm.wheel.drag\_steering: true. Off, the wheel is clicked in thirds.
dry\_hull.flood\_breath: true. Off, flood water inside a hull never drowns.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p4.list1_: melee.skill\_based\_combat: true. Off, our swords fight like vanilla swords.
firearms.fire\_on\_attack: true. Off, guns fire when right click is released.
combat.cannon\_block\_damage: true. Cannon fire also obeys mobGriefing and spawn protection.
almanac.give\_on\_first\_join: true. One Almanac for every new hand.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p5.list1_: /pirates career: your rank, standing and letter of marque.
/pirates rep: your standing with the navy, the pirates and the villagers.
/pirates waves: the sea state where you stand.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p6.list1_: /pirates law score, fine, bounty list, clear.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.ledger.p7.text1: Ship templates, trade goods and weapon timings are data files, and tags decide what never sails, what keeps water out and which foods keep or cure scurvy. A datapack can replace any of them, or add to the Almanac itself.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.not_yet.title: Not yet charted
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.not_yet.p1.text1: An honest chart leaves blank what nobody has sailed. These waters the Almanac cannot describe yet, because nobody has built them.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.not_yet.p2.list1: **Oars** to move a big ship in a flat calm.
**A ship's logbook** to record your voyages and deeds.
**Paint for the hull,** to dye her planks your own colours.
**A wanted poster** of your own, beyond the chat, the notice board and the rank box.
**Feints of your own** with the sword, and a choice of side for your cut and parry.
**Sounds of their own** for most of the work aboard.
lang.pirates_n_ships.almanac.not_yet.p2.text1: If these pages and the sea disagree, the mistake is the Almanac's. Tell whoever keeps your server.
